name: bonk-air3-meteor-cleave-v3
notes: Third pass of the air.3 concept (2026-10-17): the second pass's motion within Unity's Humanoid limits, with a cleaner left-hand path. Existing move-data clock (50 ticks, hitbox 21-36, no IASA).
character: Bonk (55 joints, five fingers; a 1.84 m greatsword fixed to the right hand as joint Weapon0 with bladeHilt and bladeEnd anchors)
image_notes: 1: the fall entry pose with the greatsword resting on the right shoulder (profile, front, three-quarter rear angle). 2: Bonk's own two-handed grip, from his Charging Double Slash (front, three-quarter, profile). 3: the second version at ticks 6, 10, 14, 16, 18, 21, 24, 28, 33 and 40, from the game camera behind him (top row) and from the side (bottom row).
description:
Downward Sweep (air.3), Bonk's committed spike, as a meteor cleave: a two-handed overhead chop down his right side that keeps going down beneath him while his body jackknifes. This is a third pass. Keep the motion of the second version (image 3): the load with the blade hanging behind his back, the whip over his right shoulder, contact beside his right knee with the deep forward fold, and the hang with the blade straight down beside his right foot, visible from the game camera. Its collarbones turned far past what Unity's Humanoid can play, so the game would have shown a different move: rebuild it with two_hand_grip for every two-handed key, and the humanoid check must pass. Also fix its left hand, which reached the grip over the top of his head and flicked up past his head on release.

Bonk is the roster's heaviest fighter and its high-jumping acrobat: a hunched brute with huge arms, short legs and a head set low between the shoulders, swinging a 1.84 m greatsword. His aerials should look heavy and acrobatic at once.

Make the sword look heavy. In the air there is no ground to push from, so the whole body swings the blade: hips and chest wind up first and unwind first; the arms follow and the blade comes last, trailing behind the hands until it whips through. The wind-up is slow and readable, the strike takes a few fast ticks, and after contact the blade's momentum carries on and drags the body after it before Bonk reins it in (overshoot, then settle): never stop the blade dead. The legs balance the swing: they tuck to wind up and swing the opposite way to the blade during the strike.

The game camera sits behind Bonk and a little above him, so a chop straight down his middle hides behind his broad back (image 3, bottom row). Bring the blade down on his right side instead: the hands travel from above his right shoulder down past his right hip, so the blade passes outside his right arm and leg, where the camera sees it.

Beats. Tick 0 is the fall pose: the sword rests on his right shoulder with the blade diagonally across his back. Ticks 1-10: the left hand swings forward around his left side and takes the grip below the right hand, in front of his chest or face, never over the top of his head (key that path). Ticks 1-14: load: lean the chest clearly back (about 30 degrees, head up), lift both hands up beside and slightly behind the right side of his head, and let the blade drop down behind his back, tip pointing down behind him. The blade goes straight from the shoulder to that hanging load and never points straight up on the way. Knees pull up in front, so the body bends backward like a drawn bow. Ticks 14-16: a moving hold while the blade sinks a little deeper behind. Ticks 16-21: the cleave: the chest jackknifes forward and the arms whip the blade over his right shoulder and down his right side; the legs kick backward as the chest folds. Contact at tick 21: both arms nearly straight, the blade pointing forward and about 45 degrees down beside his right knee. Ticks 22-30: the blade keeps sweeping down until it points almost straight down beside and below his right foot, with the arms fully extended so the hilt hangs at full reach; the torso is folded forward about 45 degrees and the legs trail behind; the blade slows as it bottoms out. Ticks 31-36: hang in that low pose, still drifting down a little. Ticks 37-48: recover: he unfolds, the left hand lets go and drops back to its fall place by his left side, staying below his head, and the right arm carries the sword back up onto the shoulder. Ticks 48-50 equal the entry pose. The blade must not cut through his body or legs.
